A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S2E navigation research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation benchmark results, real-world robot experiments, scaling studies, and ablations in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and real-world results, revised scaling experiments, and additional model and simulation ablations in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: v2 replaces EfficientNet-B0 with DINOv3, changes the transformer from four to six layers, adds image-goal conditioning and stochastic goal masking, and specifies supervision after each RAM block. The reward gains road-keeping, trajectory-similarity, and smoothness components. v2 also specifies K-means anchors instead of v1's uniform sampling, although inconsistent uniform-sampling prose remains.

E1.justification: Training coverage expands to FrodoBots-2K sidewalk trajectories from the FrodoBot platform, image/point-goal training configurations, and redesigned structured urban simulation environments. These change represented platforms and input-environment conditions. The existing RECON evaluation, 26-scene/four-task NavBench-GS benchmark, and three simulated embodiment types remain.

E2.justification: The four-task benchmark removes ZeroPolicy, ViNT*, and NoMaD*, adds matched-data CityWalker*, and drops the four-task S2E-SFT comparison. ViNT* remains in the separate RL-finetuning experiment. Appendix D.1 adds S2E-Discrete and S2E-Diffusion comparisons, while Table 3 replaces full-parameter fine-tuning with decoder-only DecFT-RL.

E3.justification: Pretraining changes from 35 to 100 hours, 30 to 100 epochs, and batch size 64 to 256; image resolution, temporal context, and prediction horizon also change. RL uses 64 rather than 256 parallel environments, and the scaling experiment extends to 750k frames. Real-world evaluation changes from eight routes across five scenarios to 25 scenarios. NavBench-GS metrics and success criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds action-representation comparisons, decoder-finetuning stability and memory analysis, a direct single-anchor versus multi-anchor navigation test, and an ablation of simulation layouts. The anchor-count study extends to 64 anchors. Conversely, v1's CLIP/DINO-v2/RADIO/EfficientNet comparison and associated trajectory analysis are removed; cross-embodiment analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 changes reported real-world repetitions from three per route to five per scenario. v2 adds shaded bands in the RAM training curves without defining their statistical meaning. The cross-embodiment table retains the same uncertainty values, with no new stated confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Many benchmark, baseline, scaling, and ablation results change. S2E's NavBench-GS success rates become 0.82/0.57/0.74/0.51 versus 0.83/0.76/0.57/0.55 for Empty/Obstacle/Pedestrian/combined tasks. Real-world wheeled/quadruped success rates become 0.51/0.55 versus 0.42/0.50. These are revised results under changed model and experimental settings, not controlled performance gains. Cross-embodiment results remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a formal feature-discrepancy definition and a gradient-flow argument for zero-initialized RAM. The displayed RAM equation also revises the residual branch's input. These are localized mathematical additions and revisions; the GMM likelihood and entropy treatment largely remain, and no theorem or proof suite is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: combining offline pretraining with RL through AGDM and RAM, introducing NavBench-GS, overcoming offline-scaling limitations, and enabling zero-shot cross-embodiment navigation. Revised methods and evidence do not materially redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving covariate shift, forgetting pretrained capabilities, gated adaptation, and computational efficiency. It removes the interpretation favoring smaller visual backbones and the warning that anchors beyond eight introduce redundancy. Limitations concerning mechanical sim-to-real discrepancies and locomotion inaccuracies are deleted, while the lack-of-3D-perception limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix E supplies new tokenization and goal-masking details, reward formulas and coefficients, and revised training hardware and timing information; reported finetuning time changes from 15 to eight hours. The former tensor-dimension architecture table and explicit parameter count disappear. v2 adds code, model-weight, and procedural-generator release plans, but the PDFs do not establish actual availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting RL forgetting and adaptation, K-means, DINOv3, FrodoBots-2K, Gaussian Splatting, and DiffusionDrive, while removing references associated with the deleted backbone study and some implementation descriptions. The main Related Work section and positioning relative to navigation foundation models remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 is substantially rewritten and reorganized around forgetting, domain shift, RAM, rewards, and training objectives. Ablations become part of the experiments section, limitations are condensed into the conclusion, and appendix material is reordered with a contents list. New acknowledgment, ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements accompany broader copyediting.

P2.justification: v2 revises the architecture diagram and scaling plots, adds sidewalk-deployment, physical-interaction, training-stability, anchor-cluster, and structured-environment visuals, and removes the visual-backbone figure. Benchmark displays are reorganized into main baseline and appendix variant tables, and the tensor-dimension table is removed. The ICLR layout also substantially reflows and relocates retained displays.

improvement.justification: More direct within-S2E comparisons, the simulation-layout ablation, expanded real-world testing, and explicit reward and tokenization details strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The gain is limited by removal of the backbone analysis and mechanical limitations, plus unresolved inconsistencies: v2 describes anchors as both uniform and K-means, and its Table 1 does not support the claim of best route completion across every task.
